summary: Both sides trace a dot along a Lissajous path with a persistence trail and all nine dials respond in the right direction, but the original's figure is a CLOSED curve that retraces itself forever (position repeats to 0.1-0.6 px) while the port's path never closes and smears the whole 16x16 grid into a speckle field within ~4 s at every dial setting.
observations: Closure is the headline divergence. Tracking the lit centroid every 0.15 s over 30 s (persistence=0, Speed=0.2, A=0.7, B=0.6, Delta=0.5, run `path-period`): the original's position repeats at lag 1.35 s with 0.10 px mean error (and at every multiple: 2.70 s / 0.20 px, 4.05 s / 0.29 px). The port has no tight repeat anywhere in the 0.45-15 s lag range - its best lag is 10.20 s at 1.35 px mean error, ~13x worse. Repeated at A=0.1/0.3/0.5/0.9 (`per-A*`): original closes at 6.75 s with 0.34-0.59 px error every time; the port's best is 0.86-1.51 px every time. The port's curve is not a rational-ratio Lissajous.

Consequence with a trail on (persistence=0.9, Speed=0.3, A/B/Delta matched, dot sizes equalized so both start at ~13 lit px - runs `shape-eq`, `A-0.1`, `A-0.7`, `delta-0`, `delta-1`): the original converges by ~4 s to a stable closed figure (a clean ellipse at A=0.7, a W/M double-loop at A=0.1, a bowtie at A=0.4) and holds it unchanged for the remaining 20 s. The port draws a recognisable arc for ~2 s, then keeps drifting and by 5-6 s the whole grid is lit random speckle; it stays that way for the rest of the run at every A and every Delta tested.
Same divergence at 48x48 (`grid48`, A=0.7): the original renders a thin, stable, dotted ellipse; the port renders coarse full-canvas speckle. So it is not a 16x16 rasterisation artefact.

Untouched defaults (`baseline`, `dump-untouched`, `mid-30`, `late-120`): original lights ~65 of 256 px - a short comet-trail sliding along a curve - with mean brightness 2.3; port lights ~230 of 256 px with mean brightness 21.8, ~10x brighter. Unchanged at t=30 s and t=120 s on both sides, so this is the steady state, not a transient.

Untouched default colour differs. Original's peak pixel is red-family throughout - [222,0,125], [148,22,0], [210,0,10], [179,16,0] - hue oscillating around 0. Port's peak is always cyan/blue with R pinned at exactly 0 - [0,182,223], [0,35,215], [0,146,209], [0,92,213] - hue around 0.55. Two different default picker colours.

Dot geometry differs. At persistence=0, Speed=0.05, matched Size (`size-*`): the original draws a HARD dot (Size 0.5 -> 2 lit px; Size 0 -> completely dark, 0 lit px), the port draws a SOFT gaussian blob with a floor (Size 0.5 -> 39 lit px; Size 0 -> still 12 lit px, peak 130). Lit-pixel counts per Size value 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1: orig 0/0/2/13/52, port 12/24/39/85/137. The port's dot is ~2-2.5x the radius at every setting and cannot be turned off.

Figure amplitude differs. Over 30 s the original's centroid spans exactly 9.1 px on both axes at A=0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 and 0.9 - a fixed, centred figure occupying ~57% of the 16 px rig. The port spans 12.2-14.5 px (75-90% of the rig) and the span varies with A.

Control names differ on 3 of 9: original has hsvPickerColor / sliderHueShift / sliderSize, port has hsvPickerDotColor / sliderHueShiftAmount / sliderDotSize (labels Color/HueShift/Size vs DotColor/HueShiftAmount/DotSize). Kinds and the other six names (sliderHueShiftSpeed, sliderPersistence, sliderSpeed, sliderA, sliderB, sliderDelta) match.

Per-frame step rate roughly matches at low Speed - 0.6 px/frame on both at Speed=0.05, and 1.0-1.7 px/frame on both at Speed=0.3 - so the port is not obviously frame-rate coupled relative to the original; the divergence is in the trajectory's shape, not its rate.
Seed-independent on both sides: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 give mean brightness 2/2/2 (orig) and 23/23/23 (port) with the same look, so nothing here is a one-seed fluke.
No error on either side - both compile and run clean, wantsSensors false on both, no runtime errors, port zeroMotionFrames 1/120. The port is alive, just structurally wrong.
The survey (60 s @ 5 fps) plus 30 s and 120 s parked windows showed no mode rotation on either side: both are statistically stationary after ~2 s, so there is no second regime hiding the match.

dials.name: hsvPickerColor / hsvPickerDotColor
dials.origEffect: Sets the dot's base hue; picker h=0 renders hue 0.000 at the peak pixel, h=0.5 renders cyan
dials.portEffect: Same - h=0 renders hue 0.000, h=0.5 renders cyan; strongest dial in the probe (maxDelta 33.3)

dials.name: sliderHueShift / sliderHueShiftAmount
dials.origEffect: At 0 the hue is frozen at the picker value. At 0.5 the peak hue starts at 0.758 and walks ~0.0145/s; at 1 it starts at 0.517 and walks ~0.029/s
dials.portEffect: Same starting offsets (0.763 at 0.5, 0.528 at 1 - within 0.01 of the original) but the walk is ~1.7x faster: ~0.025/s at 0.5 and ~0.050/s at 1

dials.name: sliderHueShiftSpeed
dials.origEffect: Adds a wobble on top of the hue walk; raising it makes the peak hue jitter non-monotonically instead of drifting smoothly
dials.portEffect: Same character of change - wobble appears and grows with the setting

dials.name: sliderPersistence
dials.origEffect: Trail length. Lit px at t=8 s (Size 0.75, Speed 0.3) for 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1: 13/38/96/211/236
dials.portEffect: Same direction, but saturates almost immediately: 131/240/253/256/256 - the port is at full grid coverage by persistence 0.5 where the original is at 38%

dials.name: sliderSize / sliderDotSize
dials.origEffect: Hard-edged dot; lit px for 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 = 0/0/2/13/52, i.e. the dot vanishes entirely below ~0.4
dials.portEffect: Soft gaussian blob with a floor; lit px = 12/24/39/85/137, never smaller than ~12 px even at 0

dials.name: sliderSpeed
dials.origEffect: Traversal rate; centroid step/frame at 0/0.1 = 0.33/0.56 px, rising steeply above 0.5
dials.portEffect: Same direction, ~1.3-1.4x faster at the low end (0.49/0.72 px) and rising less steeply

dials.name: sliderA
dials.origEffect: Selects the figure: 0.1 gives a W/M double-loop, 0.4 a bowtie, 0.7 a plain ellipse - each a distinct CLOSED curve, always spanning 9.1 px on both axes
dials.portEffect: Changes the early arc's shape but no value produces a closed figure - all of 0.1/0.3/0.5/0.7/0.9 fill the grid with speckle within ~5 s; span varies 12.2-14.5 px

dials.name: sliderB
dials.origEffect: Second frequency term; combines with A to pick the closed figure (held at 0.6 for all comparisons)
dials.portEffect: Responsive in the probe (maxDelta 20.1) but, like A, never yields a closed figure

dials.name: sliderDelta
dials.origEffect: Phase offset - rotates/reshapes the closed figure (0 gives an open-lobed loop, 1 a tighter crossed figure) while keeping it closed and stable
dials.portEffect: Alters the early arc but the figure still never closes at any Delta (0/0.25/0.75/1 all end as full-grid speckle)

feedback: PRIMARY FIX - make the traced path close. The original's dot returns to its exact starting position on a fixed period (1.35 s at Speed=0.2/A=0.7/B=0.6, 6.75 s at A=0.1/0.3/0.5/0.9, mean position error 0.1-0.6 px) so the persistence trail retraces one curve forever. The port's position never repeats better than 1.35 px over a 15 s lag scan, so its trail sweeps new ground every cycle and fills the rig. Whatever the port derives its two frequencies from, they need to land on an exact small-integer ratio (the original's behaviour is consistent with the A and B dials selecting integer frequencies - A=0.7/B=0.6 gives a 1:1 ellipse, A=0.1/B=0.6 gives a 3-lobe W) rather than on a continuum.

Shrink the dot and give it a hard edge. At the same Size value the port lights 3-20x as many pixels as the original (Size 0.5: 39 px vs 2 px; Size 0.75: 85 vs 13; Size 1: 137 vs 52). The original's dot is essentially a single hard pixel at mid Size and disappears completely at Size <= 0.4; the port's is a soft gaussian that still covers 12 px at Size 0. Reduce the radius by roughly 2-2.5x and let the low end of the dial reach zero.

Rein in persistence. Matched at Size 0.75 / Speed 0.3 the port hits full grid coverage (253-256 of 256 lit) at Persistence 0.5 where the original is at 96 - the port's trail decays far too slowly across the whole dial range. Target roughly the original's lit-pixel curve 13/38/96/211/236 for Persistence 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1.
Halve the hue-walk rate. Starting hues match within 0.01, but the port's hue advances ~1.7x too fast at every HueShift setting (0.025/s vs 0.0145/s at HueShift=0.5; 0.050/s vs 0.029/s at HueShift=1).

Fix the untouched default colour: the original comes up red-family (peak RGB like [222,0,125] / [210,0,10] / [179,16,0], hue near 0), the port comes up cyan/blue with R pinned at 0 (peak like [0,146,209], hue near 0.55). The picker itself works identically on both sides, so this is purely the default value the pattern starts with.

Reduce the figure's amplitude: the original's centre-of-light spans exactly 9.1 px on both axes on a 16 px grid (~57% of the rig) at every A value; the port spans 12-14.5 px and the span drifts with A.

Rename three controls to match the original's surface: hsvPickerDotColor -> hsvPickerColor (label Color), sliderHueShiftAmount -> sliderHueShift (label HueShift), sliderDotSize -> sliderSize (label Size). The other six names and all nine kinds already match.
